CHART CONTROLS ▸ GUIDE ▸

How do different measures of academic proficiency relate?

Every dot is one California public high school. Click CHART CONTROLS above to pick a measure for each axis, the year, and the view — the view buttons spin the plane flat or tilt it forward so either axis collapses into a histogram. Click any dot to tag its school and follow it across views; double-click anywhere to clear all tags. Scroll over the plot to zoom; a note appears in the corner to reset.

Every measure on this page is a real published school-level figure: CAASPP results, A–G completion, and the older STAR (CST), CAHSEE, AP, SAT, and ACT school reports from the California Department of Education; average GPAs of UC freshman applicants from UC’s admissions-by-school data; and average GPAs of CSU entering freshmen from CSU’s Student Origins dashboards. Schools are matched across sources using the project’s school-code crosswalk. A school appears in a year only if the source published a value for it, so the set of dots changes as you move the year slider or switch measures.
